title: Gaussian distribution increments
statement: For all real numbers $a$ and $b$, the increment of the standard Gaussian distribution function satisfies $\Phi(b)-\Phi(a)=\int_a^b\varphi(x)\,dx$, where the interval integral is signed.
replaced:
Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$. For any real $a,b$, with no ordering assumption, one has
\[
\Phi(b)-\Phi(a)=\int_a^b\varphi(x)\,dx,
\]
where the interval integral is signed, so that $\int_a^b=-\int_b^a$ when $b<a$.
